A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves attach at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or whorled arrangement visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem, not clustered at the apex)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf has a single blade without subdivisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapers to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapers to a narrow base, wedge-shaped)

    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short compared to leaf blade)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and brown, with visible bark, typical of woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs visible on stem surface, especially in close-up images)
    19. Stem color: brown (stem is brownish, with some greenish areas possibly due to moss or algae)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): ridged (stem surface shows slight ridges or grooves, not smooth)

    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no milky sap or latex visible in any images)
